Look at evidence:

**Gaps in failing attempts:**
- **A (6 attempts: a2,a3,a4,a5,a6,a9)** — applied EU-country selection filter to the *projected* `?countries` binding, so output listed only EU countries. Reference rows (`"GR, US"`, `"US, ES, CH"`) prove countries column not restricted to selection criterion. Both passers (a7,a8) bound `?country` unfiltered and gated EU via separate `FILTER EXISTS`. Biggest by count.
- **B (a1,a9,a10)** — role prefix `"Professor of"` instead of `"Professor"`; brittle on held-out roles.
- **C (a1,a10)** — `OPTIONAL`+`!BOUND(?grad)` vs `FILTER NOT EXISTS { grad <= ref }` graduation semantics.

Gap A dominant. But gap A **is** rejected lesson `candidate-r2-scope-leak` (sha 1e93189412739dd0) — same mechanism, same task, same trigger ("selection condition on attribute that is also output → gate via separate existence check, do not filter projected attribute"). Rule 8 blocks re-derivation; that rejection was not trigger-overreach, it was null-on-base.

Remaining gaps B and C are smaller, and heterogeneous with different fixes (string-prefix strictness vs multi-valued-property aggregation semantics) — both also fixable only by SPARQL/domain mechanics, which rules 3/3b forbid. Note a1 and a10 got gap A *right* and still failed, so A alone would not flip all failers anyway.

Abstain.
